headline: New EU greenwashing rules active; Chinese supply chain risks rise
summary: The EU's anti-greenwashing directive has entered into force, impacting consumer product marketing. Meanwhile, labour complaints from China highlight supply chain risks, and member states are rapidly transposing pay transparency rules. You must also prepare for upcoming CSRD and Machinery Regulation deadlines.

items.title: EU anti-greenwashing rules enter into force
items.what: The Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition Directive has entered into force, banning misleading environmental claims and unsubstantiated sustainability labels.
items.meaning: As a consumer brand, you must ensure all environmental claims on your power tools and packaging are fully substantiated and compliant.
items.action: Audit all current marketing and packaging claims for compliance.

sources.title: New EU Anti-Greenwashing Rules Enter into Force

items.title: Chinese workers raise labour complaints to EU
items.what: Chinese workers submitted complaints to the EU regarding severe overtime, highlighting systemic labour risks in Chinese manufacturing.
items.meaning: With 200 Chinese suppliers, you face increased reputational and compliance risks under EU import and reporting rules.
items.action: Review supplier audit reports specifically for working hours and overtime compliance.

sources.title: Brutale Überstunden-Kultur: Chinas Arbeiter beschweren sich bei der EU

items.title: EU clarifies Machinery Regulation implementation rules
items.what: The EU published a corrigendum to Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, clarifying harmonised rules ahead of its January 2027 application.
items.meaning: As the legal manufacturer of power tools, you must ensure your products and technical files align with these clarified requirements.
items.action: Review technical documentation against the updated regulation.

items.title: Member states accelerate Pay Transparency transposition
items.what: Slovakia, Greece, and Malta have transposed the EU Pay Transparency Directive into national law.
items.meaning: With over 1,000 employees, you must prepare for strict gender pay gap reporting as national rollouts progress.
items.action: Assess HR readiness for gender pay gap reporting.

items.title: EU updates EUDR customs codes and guidance
items.what: The EU updated customs codes and Information System guidance for the Deforestation Regulation, which applies from late December 2026.
items.meaning: You must ensure any wood or paper packaging used for your imported finished goods complies with EUDR.
items.action: Verify EUDR compliance for all product packaging with suppliers.
